theorems.name: First-to-Default Spread Is the Sum of Single-Name Hazards
theorems.description: For a basket of jointly independent exponential default times τ_i ~ Exp(rates i), the first-to-default credit spread — read off the measure of the basket survival event, −log μ(min_i τ_i > t)/t for t > 0 — equals Σ rates: basket intensity is the sum of single-name intensities, so FtD spreads are additive under independence. Dependent default times are not treated.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Credit.FirstToDefault

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory MathFin

theorem first_to_default_spread_thm
    {Ω : Type*} {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω}
    {n : ℕ} {rates : Fin n → ℝ} {τ : Fin n → Ω → ℝ}
    (hrates_pos : ∀ i, 0 < rates i)
    (hexp_law : ∀ i, Measure.map (τ i) μ = expMeasure (rates i))
    (hindep : iIndepFun τ μ)
    (hmeas : ∀ i, Measurable (τ i))
    (hn : 0 < n) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    -Real.log ((μ {ω | t < Finset.univ.inf' ⟨⟨0, hn⟩, Finset.mem_univ _⟩
        (fun i : Fin n => τ i ω)}).toReal) / t
      = ∑ i, rates i :=
  MathFin.firstToDefault_spread_eq_sum_hazards hrates_pos hexp_law hindep hmeas hn ht

metadata.reference: First-to-default baskets under independent reduced-form intensities (Lando 2004 Ch 5; Duffie-Singleton 2003)

theorems.name: Credit Spread as Time-Averaged Hazard
theorems.description: Under time-varying hazard h(u), the credit spread c(T) = -log(S(T))/T = H(T)/T where H is the cumulative hazard. The spread is the time-averaged hazard.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Credit.HazardCurve

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- **Credit spread = time-averaged hazard** — definitional given
    `S := exp(−H)` (`Real.log_exp`); paired below with the substantive FTC
    recovery that grounds the model. -/
theorem creditSpread_eq_time_avg_hazard_thm {h : ℝ → ℝ} {T : ℝ} (hT : 0 < T) :
    -Real.log (MathFin.hazardSurvival h T) / T = MathFin.cumHazard h T / T :=
  MathFin.creditSpread_eq_time_avg_hazard hT

/-- **Hazard recovered from the survival curve** (the substantive direction):
    `h(t) = −d/dt log S(t)` for continuous `h`, by the FTC through the
    `ExponentialDiscount` principle. -/
theorem hazard_recovers_from_survival_thm {h : ℝ → ℝ} (t : ℝ)
    (hh : Continuous h) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => -(Real.log (MathFin.hazardSurvival h s))) (h t) t :=
  MathFin.hazard_eq_neg_log_deriv_survival t hh

metadata.reference: Hazard curve and credit spread (Lando, Credit Risk Modeling)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. The snippet exports both directions honestly split: the spread identity −log S(T)/T = H(T)/T is definitional given S := exp(−H) (Real.log_exp), and the substantive content is the FTC recovery hazard_eq_neg_log_deriv_survival (h(t) = −d/dt log S(t) for continuous h), also exported. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: KMV-Merton risk-neutral probability of default = Q(V_T ≤ F)
theorems.description: Under the Merton structural model with the firm value's risk-neutral law (BSCallHyp), the KMV default probability kmvPD equals the actual risk-neutral default probability 1 − Q({V_T > F}) — the genuine probabilistic content (via the BS risk-neutral exercise probability), not the algebraic Φ-symmetry identity.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Credit.KMVMertonStructural

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open MathFin

theorem kmv_pd_eq_risk_neutral_default_thm
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {Q : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
    [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {V_0 F r σ_V T : ℝ} {Z : Ω → ℝ}
    (hV : 0 < V_0) (hF : 0 < F) (h : MathFin.BSCallHyp Q V_0 F r σ_V T Z) :
    MathFin.kmvPD V_0 F r σ_V T =
      1 - (Q {ω | MathFin.bsTerminal V_0 r σ_V T (Z ω) > F}).toReal :=
  MathFin.kmvPD_eq_one_sub_survival_probability hV hF h

theorems.name: KMV-Merton Survival Probability = Φ(d_2^KMV)
theorems.description: The probabilistic survival statement of the KMV–Merton model: under risk-neutral lognormal firm-value dynamics, Q({V_T > F}).toReal = Φ(DD) — the measure of the no-default event equals the standard-normal CDF of the distance to default (survival_probability_eq_Phi_distanceToDefault), routed through the lognormal tail computation riskNeutralProb_S_T_gt_K and kmvDistanceToDefault_eq_bsd2.

import MathFin.Models.Credit.KMVMertonStructural

theorem kmv_survival_probability_eq_Phi_dd_thm

theorems.name: One-Factor Default Model Is the Gaussian Factor Copula
theorems.description: In the one-factor Gaussian threshold model (F and ε₁, …, εₙ independent standard normals, asset correlation ρ ∈ [0, 1), default probability π ∈ (0, 1)), the probability that all n names default, P(√ρ F + √(1 − ρ) εᵢ ≤ Φ⁻¹(π) for all i), equals C(π, …, π) for the one-factor Gaussian copula C with factor loading √ρ.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Risk.Credit.OneFactorCopula

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter Topology
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
open MathFin

/-- All `n` names of the one-factor model default together with probability `C(π, …, π)`, `C` the
Gaussian factor copula at loading `√ρ`. -/
theorem oneFactor_joint_default_eq_gaussianFactorCopula {n : ℕ} {Ω : Type*}
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {π ρ : ℝ} {F : Ω → ℝ}
    {ε : Fin n → Ω → ℝ} (hF : HasLaw F (gaussianReal 0 1) P)
    (hε : ∀ i, HasLaw (ε i) (gaussianReal 0 1) P) (hεind : iIndepFun ε P)
    (hFε : F ⟂ᵢ[P] fun ω i ↦ ε i ω) (hπ : π ∈ Ioo 0 1) (hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ) (hρ1 : ρ < 1) :
    P.real (⋂ i, {ω | √ρ * F ω + √(1 - ρ) * ε i ω ≤ PhiInv π}) =
      (gaussianFactorCopula n √ρ).real (Iic fun _ ↦ π) :=
  MathFin.oneFactor_measureReal_iInter_default_eq_gaussianFactorCopula hF hε hεind hFε hπ hρ0 hρ1

metadata.reference: J. Hull and A. White, "Valuation of a CDO and an n-th to default CDS without Monte Carlo simulation", Journal of Derivatives 12(2) (2004) (the one-factor Gaussian copula model); QRM Exercise Book Ex. 11.9 (joint default probabilities of the one-factor model)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.oneFactor_measureReal_iInter_default_eq_gaussianFactorCopula (MathFin/Risk/Credit/OneFactorCopula.lean). SCOPE: both sides are shown equal to the mixture integral ∫ p(x)ⁿ dN(0,1)(x) (oneFactor_measureReal_iInter_default, applied once on the given space and once on the canonical factor space where Sklar's theorem gives the copula). Only the diagonal point (π, …, π) and identical default probabilities are covered; heterogeneous thresholds are not stated.

theorems.name: Two-Name Joint Default in the One-Factor Gaussian Model
theorems.description: In the one-factor Gaussian threshold model with asset correlation ρ ∈ [0, 1) (F and the εᵢ independent standard normals), two distinct names default together with probability N₂(Φ⁻¹(π), Φ⁻¹(π); ρ), the standard bivariate normal CDF at correlation ρ. Holds for every real π (Φ⁻¹ is the library's PhiInv).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Risk.Credit.OneFactorCopula

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter Topology
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
open MathFin

/-- Two names of the one-factor model default together with probability
`N₂(Φ⁻¹(π), Φ⁻¹(π); ρ)`. -/
theorem oneFactor_pairwise_default_eq_bivariateNormalCDF {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {π ρ : ℝ} {F : Ω → ℝ}
    {ε : ι → Ω → ℝ} (hF : HasLaw F (gaussianReal 0 1) P)
    (hε : ∀ i, HasLaw (ε i) (gaussianReal 0 1) P) (hεind : iIndepFun ε P)
    (hFε : F ⟂ᵢ[P] fun ω i ↦ ε i ω) (hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ) (hρ1 : ρ < 1) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    P.real ({ω | √ρ * F ω + √(1 - ρ) * ε i ω ≤ PhiInv π} ∩
        {ω | √ρ * F ω + √(1 - ρ) * ε j ω ≤ PhiInv π}) =
      bivariateNormalCDF (PhiInv π) (PhiInv π) ρ :=
  MathFin.oneFactor_measureReal_inter_default hF hε hεind hFε hρ0 hρ1 hij

theorems.name: Pairs of the One-Factor Gaussian Latent Vector Are Bivariate Normal
theorems.description: For the one-factor Gaussian latent vector Xᵢ = ρ Z₀ + √(1 − ρ²) Zᵢ with Z₀, Z₁, …, Zₙ independent standard normals and loading ρ ∈ [−1, 1], each pair (Xᵢ, Xⱼ) with i ≠ j has the standard bivariate normal law with correlation ρ².

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter Topology

/-- Each pair of latent coordinates of the one-factor Gaussian model is standard bivariate normal
with correlation `ρ²`. -/
theorem gaussianFactorVec_pair_law {n : ℕ} {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ρ ∈ Icc (-1) 1) {i j : Fin n}
    (hij : i ≠ j) :
    (stdNormalFactors n).map (fun z ↦ (gaussianFactorVec ρ z i, gaussianFactorVec ρ z j)) =
      bivariateNormalLaw (ρ ^ 2) :=
  MathFin.map_pair_gaussianFactorVec hρ hij

theorems.name: CreditMetrics Thresholds Reproduce the Transition Matrix
theorems.description: For a row-stochastic transition matrix P on m ratings, take in row i the thresholds Φ⁻¹ of the cumulative row sums ∑_{k<j} P i k (−∞ and +∞ at the ends). Standard normal threshold migration with these thresholds has transition matrix exactly P.

import MathFin.Risk.Credit.CreditMetrics

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter Topology
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
open MathFin

/-- Standard normal threshold migration with the `Φ⁻¹`-calibrated thresholds reproduces `P`. -/
theorem creditMetrics_threshold_calibration {m : ℕ} {P : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
    (hP : P ∈ Matrix.rowStochastic ℝ (Fin m)) :
    thresholdMatrix (gaussianReal 0 1) (gaussianThresholds P) = P :=
  MathFin.thresholdMatrix_gaussianThresholds hP

metadata.reference: CreditMetrics Technical Document (J.P. Morgan 1997), ch. 8 (asset-return thresholds of a rating transition matrix)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.thresholdMatrix_gaussianThresholds (MathFin/Risk/Credit/CreditMetrics.lean). SCOPE: the threshold of a cumulative probability c is ⊥ for c ≤ 0, ⊤ for c ≥ 1 and Φ⁻¹(c) otherwise (gaussianThreshold), so zero-probability buckets are handled; the standard normal mass between consecutive thresholds is the difference of cumulative sums. One obligor's marginal migration; the ordering of ratings is the threshold order (lowest returns first).

theorems.name: CreditMetrics Default Covariance of Two Obligors
theorems.description: Two obligors in ratings i and k migrate by the Φ⁻¹-calibrated CreditMetrics thresholds of a transition matrix P, and their latent returns are standard bivariate normal with asset correlation r ∈ [−1, 1]. If their default probabilities P i 0 and P k 0 (the lowest bucket) lie in (0, 1), the covariance of their default indicators is N₂(Φ⁻¹(P i 0), Φ⁻¹(P k 0); r) − P i 0 · P k 0.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Risk.Credit.CreditMetrics

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter Topology
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
open MathFin

/-- The covariance of the default indicators of two obligors with correlated returns is
`N₂(Φ⁻¹(p₁), Φ⁻¹(p₂); r) − p₁ p₂`. -/
theorem creditMetrics_default_covariance {m : ℕ} {P : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ}
    {i k : Fin (m + 1)} (hi : P i 0 ∈ Ioo 0 1) (hk : P k 0 ∈ Ioo 0 1) {r : ℝ}
    (hr : r ^ 2 ≤ 1) :
    cov[(Prod.fst ⁻¹' ratingBucket (gaussianThresholds P i) 0).indicator 1,
        (Prod.snd ⁻¹' ratingBucket (gaussianThresholds P k) 0).indicator 1;
        bivariateNormalLaw r] =
      bivariateNormalCDF (PhiInv (P i 0)) (PhiInv (P k 0)) r - P i 0 * P k 0 :=
  MathFin.covariance_indicator_default_gaussianThresholds hi hk hr

metadata.reference: CreditMetrics Technical Document (J.P. Morgan 1997), ch. 8 (joint default probability from asset correlation)

SCOPE: the lowest calibrated bucket is (−∞, Φ⁻¹(P i 0)] (ratingBucket_gaussianThresholds_zero); the covariance of two indicators is P(A ∩ B) − P(A)P(B) (covariance_indicator_one, MathFin/Probability/Dependence/HoeffdingCovariance.lean); the joint default probability is N₂ (measureReal_default_prod_gaussianThresholds) and the margins are standard normal. Only joint default is covered; joint migration to other buckets is not stated. The asset correlation r is a parameter, not estimated.

theorems.name: Default Covariance Under a Common Shock
theorems.description: For independent exponential T₁, T₂, T₃ with rates λ₁, λ₂, λ₃ > 0 and default times Xⱼ = min(Tⱼ, T₃), the default indicators 𝟙{X₁ ≤ s} and 𝟙{X₂ ≤ t} have covariance exp(−(λ₁ + λ₃)s − (λ₂ + λ₃)t) · (exp(λ₃ min(s, t)) − 1) for s, t ≥ 0.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Probability.Dependence.MarshallOlkin

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter Topology
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
open MathFin

/-- The default-indicator covariance of the Marshall–Olkin common-shock model. -/
theorem marshallOlkin_default_covariance {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {T : Fin 3 → Ω → ℝ} {rate : Fin 3 → ℝ} (hrate : ∀ i, 0 < rate i)
    (hT : ∀ i, HasLaw (T i) (expMeasure (rate i)) P) (hind : iIndepFun T P) {s t : ℝ}
    (hs : 0 ≤ s) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    cov[{ω | min (T 0 ω) (T 2 ω) ≤ s}.indicator 1, {ω | min (T 1 ω) (T 2 ω) ≤ t}.indicator 1;
        P] =
      Real.exp (-((rate 0 + rate 2) * s) - (rate 1 + rate 2) * t) *
        (Real.exp (rate 2 * min s t) - 1) :=
  MathFin.covariance_indicator_marshallOlkin hrate hT hind hs ht

SCOPE: the covariance of the two indicators is computed on the joint law of (X₁, X₂) by covariance_indicator_one and measureReal_inter_sub_mul_compl (MathFin/Probability/Dependence/HoeffdingCovariance.lean), then read off the joint survival function marshallOlkin_survival and the exponential margins. theorems.description: For Λ ∼ Gamma(a, r) (shape a > 0, rate r > 0, Mathlib's gammaMeasure) and s < r, E[exp(sΛ)] = (r / (r − s))^a.

theorems.name: CreditRisk+ Sector Loss MGF (Mixture Form)
theorems.description: For i.i.d. losses Xᵢ with common MGF M_X(t) (Mathlib's mgf, which is 0 where the MGF is infinite) and a Poisson default count whose intensity is mixed against Gamma(a, r), a, r > 0: if M_X(t) < r + 1, the compound-Poisson MGF of the n-loss sum integrated against Poisson(λ) and then against Gamma(a, r) equals (r / (r − (M_X(t) − 1)))^a. Stated as the iterated mixture integral; the mixed count and the sector loss are not constructed as random variables.

theorems.name: CVA With Gaussian Exposure and No Wrong-Way Risk

Only the marginal laws of Vₛ enter; no exposure dynamics are modelled.

theorems.name: Large Homogeneous Portfolio Stop-Loss in Closed Form

    (D : ℝ≥0 → ℝ) (X : Unit → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (a d : ℝ) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    (trancheLeg a d T).value Q (fun t _ ↦ D t) X
      = D T * ∫ ω, tranchePayoff a d (X () T ω) ∂Q :=
  value_trancheLeg Q D X a d T

theorems.name: Merton's Structural Credit Model Is a Market: Equity Is a Call, Debt Is the Firm Less the Call, Default Probability Is kmvPD
theorems.description: Let the firm's assets be the Black-Scholes market of a pre-Brownian motion W (BlackScholes.market: spot V0 > 0, physical drift m, rate r, volatility sigma > 0) and debt of face F > 0 fall due at T <= H, T > 0. The Girsanov measure Q of the constant market price of risk (m - r)/sigma at horizon H is a pricing measure of that market (Market.IsPricingMeasure); under Q the market price (Market.price) of the equity, the European call on the assets with strike F, is V0 Phi(d1) - F e^{-rT} Phi(d2); the market price of the defaultable zero-coupon bond (defaultableZCB F T, paying min(V_T, F) at T) is V0 minus the equity price; and Q(V_T <= F) = kmvPD V0 F r sigma T = Phi(-d2). Default is the event at the maturity T: first-passage (Black-Cox) default, coupons, and a stochastic rate are not covered, and that Q is the only pricing measure is not claimed.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Credit.MertonMarket

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts MathFin.Contracts.BlackScholes
open scoped NNReal

/-- Merton's structural model as a Black-Scholes market: the Girsanov measure is a pricing measure,
the equity is the Black-Scholes call, the defaultable bond is the firm less the equity, and the
default probability is `kmvPD`. -/
theorem merton_structural_market {Ω : Type*} [mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω] {W : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ}
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hW : IsPreBrownianReal W μ)
    (hWmeas : ∀ t, Measurable (W t)) {V₀ F m r σ : ℝ} {T H : ℝ≥0} (hTH : T ≤ H) (hV₀ : 0 < V₀)
    (hF : 0 < F) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < (T : ℝ)) :
    (market μ hWmeas V₀ m r σ).IsPricingMeasure T
        (constGirsanovMeasure hW hWmeas ((m - r) / σ) H) ∧
      (market μ hWmeas V₀ m r σ).price (constGirsanovMeasure hW hWmeas ((m - r) / σ) H)
          (europeanCall F T)
        = V₀ * Phi (bsd1 V₀ F r σ T) - F * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 V₀ F r σ T) ∧
      (market μ hWmeas V₀ m r σ).price (constGirsanovMeasure hW hWmeas ((m - r) / σ) H)
          (defaultableZCB F T)
        = V₀ - (V₀ * Phi (bsd1 V₀ F r σ T) - F * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 V₀ F r σ T)) ∧
      (constGirsanovMeasure hW hWmeas ((m - r) / σ) H).real
          {ω | (market μ hWmeas V₀ m r σ).asset () T ω ≤ F}
        = kmvPD V₀ F r σ T :=
  Merton.merton_market hW hWmeas hTH hV₀ hF hσ hT

metadata.reference: R. C. Merton, On the pricing of corporate debt: the risk structure of interest rates, J. Finance 29 (1974) 449-470; D. Lando, Credit Risk Modeling, Princeton (2004), sec. 2.2
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. merton_market in MathFin/Models/Credit/MertonMarket.lean: the pricing measure and the call price are isPricingMeasure_constGirsanovMeasure and price_europeanCall_constGirsanovMeasure (MathFin/Models/BlackScholes/Market.lean); the debt price is price_defaultableZCB_add_price_europeanCall (min(V_T, F) + (V_T - F)^+ = V_T, integrable by the martingale property, and the price of the claim paying V_T is V0 by Market.IsPricingMeasure.price_pay_obs); the default probability is kmvPD_eq_one_sub_survival_probability_via_brownian read on the Brownian motion B^theta of the Girsanov measure, the market asset being Q-almost surely the risk-neutral asset. SCOPE: default only at the maturity T, one asset (the firm), constant rate and volatility, Brownian motion without path continuity; no uniqueness of the pricing measure.
